definition.name: TOPO_RPAR
definition.component_coordinate: Owner-preserving residual/column incidence hypergraph canonicalized under local column permutations.
definition.cell_label: F if frontier-relative depth d=0; O if d>0 is odd; E if d>0 is even.

findings.statement: TOPO_RPAR is scalar-exact with zero contradictions on all three demanding carriers 5x3-k3, 4x4-k4, and 6x3-k3.
Absolute positive release depth is not required by the tested scalar evaluator: it is sufficient to distinguish immediate frontier cells from delayed cells and then retain only delayed-depth parity.

On 4x4-k4, TOPO_DPAR leaves 16 contradictions and TOPO_D012 leaves 12, while TOPO_RPAR closes all contradictions. The load-bearing distinction is specifically frontier status plus parity among positive release depths.

On 4x4-k4, TOPO_RPAR adds only 289 structural dimensions beyond affine versus 422 in the complete degree-2 space, yet remains scalar-exact. The omitted 133 structural directions are scalar-redundant in the tested corpus.
TOPO_RPAR is the first tested release-semantic pair coordinate coarser than exact REL_INC that is scalar-exact across every demanding carrier.

nonclaims: TOPO_RPAR is not yet fresh-qualified on a carrier that independently requires non-affine interaction.
The two scalar syndrome coefficient functions over TOPO_RPAR have not yet been derived.
next_question: Does frozen TOPO_RPAR remain scalar-exact on a predeclared fresh geometry whose affine model independently fails?
